# GitHub Repository Metadata & README Extractor

Pull structured metadata for any public GitHub repository — stars, forks, topics, license, language breakdown, and the README text — either from a GitHub search query or a list of repository URLs you already have. Supplying a personal access token is optional and only raises how many repositories you can pull per run.

## What this actor does

- **Search mode** — run any GitHub search query (`stars:>10000 language:python`, `topic:llm`, `user:apify`) and get up to 1000 matching repositories, each fully enriched
- **Direct mode** — supply a list of `github.com/owner/repo` URLs and fetch them directly
- **README text** — fetched and decoded inline, truncated at 500 KB for very large files
- **Topics and language breakdown** — the repository's topic tags and a byte count per programming language, each toggleable
- Fields a repository doesn't have (e.g. `homepage`, `license`) are omitted from its record rather than returned empty

## Output per repository

- `id`, `name`, `fullName`, `htmlUrl` — identity and canonical URL
- `owner` — `login`, `id`, `avatarUrl`, `htmlUrl`, `type`
- `description`, `homepage`, `primaryLanguage`
- `stars`, `forks`, `watchers`, `openIssues`, `size` (KB)
- `topics` — array of topic tags, when `includeTopics` is enabled
- `license` — `spdxId`, `name`, `url`
- `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `pushedAt`
- `isFork`, `isArchived`, `isDisabled`, `isTemplate` — status flags
- `defaultBranch`
- `readme` — decoded README text, truncated at 500 KB, when `includeReadme` is enabled
- `languages` — byte count per language, when `includeLanguages` is enabled
- `scrapedAt` — ISO timestamp of the scrape

When a specific repository can't be fetched, the actor emits an error record instead with `type: "github_repo_intelligence_error"`, a `reason` code (`rate_limit`, `not_found`, `invalid_url`, `search_failed`, `no_results`, `fetch_failed`), a `message`, the `repoIdentifier` that failed, and `scrapedAt` — so one bad URL doesn't stop the rest of the run.

## Input

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | `search` | `search` to run a GitHub search query, or `direct` to fetch a list of URLs |
| `searchQuery` | string | `stars:>10000 language:python` | GitHub search query (mode=search) |
| `repositoryUrls` | array | – | Repository URLs to fetch (mode=direct) |
| `sortBy` | string | `stars` | `stars`, `forks`, `updated`, or `help-wanted-issues` (mode=search) |
| `maxResults` | integer | `30` | Cap on repositories returned (1–1000) |
| `includeReadme` | boolean | `true` | Fetch and include each repository's README |
| `includeTopics` | boolean | `true` | Include the repository's topic tags |
| `includeLanguages` | boolean | `true` | Include the per-language byte breakdown |
| `githubToken` | string | – | Optional personal access token to raise your request budget |

### Example: search for popular LLM projects

```json
{
  "mode": "search",
  "searchQuery": "topic:llm stars:>500 language:python",
  "sortBy": "stars",
  "maxResults": 200
}
```

### Example: fetch a known list of repositories

```json
{
  "mode": "direct",
  "repositoryUrls": [
    "https://github.com/apify/crawlee",
    "https://github.com/apify/actor-templates"
  ]
}
```

### Example: metadata only, no README or language breakdown

```json
{
  "mode": "search",
  "searchQuery": "language:rust stars:>5000",
  "includeReadme": false,
  "includeLanguages": false,
  "maxResults": 500
}
```

## Use cases

- **Ecosystem mapping** — enumerate every repository tagged `topic:llm` or `topic:web3` to build a competitive map
- **Dependency due diligence** — gather license, archived status, and push cadence for a list of libraries you depend on
- **Leaderboards and dashboards** — rank a set of repositories by stars, forks, or recent activity
- **Market research** — compare language mix and topic distribution across a population of related projects
- **Downstream analysis pipelines** — seed a static-analysis or ML pipeline with enriched repo metadata and README text

## FAQ

**Do I need a GitHub token?** Not for small runs — a handful of repositories works without one. For larger runs, supply a personal access token to raise your hourly request budget significantly; create a classic token with the `public_repo` scope at github.com/settings/tokens.

**Why would I turn off `includeReadme`, `includeTopics`, or `includeLanguages`?** Each one adds an extra fetch per repository; disabling what you don't need lets a single run cover far more repositories within the same request budget.

**Do I need a proxy?** No — GitHub's API access isn't IP-rate-limited in a way that requires one.

**Can I scrape private repositories?** Yes, as long as the `githubToken` you supply has access to them — a classic token with `repo` scope covers all private repositories your account can read.

**Why are some fields missing from my output?** Only fields with real data are included — a repository without a homepage simply has no `homepage` key, rather than a `null`.

**How large can a README get?** READMEs are truncated at 500 KB of decoded text with a `...[truncated]` marker, which covers the vast majority of real-world READMEs in full.

**Can search return more than 1000 results?** No — that's GitHub's own hard cap on search results. For a larger universe, split the query into ranges (e.g. `stars:1000..5000`, then `stars:500..999`) and run once per range.

**What happens if one repository fails?** The actor emits an error record for that repository and continues with the rest of the batch, so one deleted or private URL doesn't stop the run.

**Is this affiliated with GitHub?** No — this is an independent actor built on GitHub's public REST API; it is not operated by GitHub.
